posts.name: Envisioner
posts.cooked:
Foote:

Ommitron is no pushover. He is certainly much more threatening than gloomy or ambuscade.

I've fought him twice, once on advanced, and both times Visionary made him her female-dog.  He doesn't have enough minions, his Components are easily destroyed, most of his effects don't fire until the second turn, TechSing does nothing against most Heroes since only a few of them are heavily into Equipment (I think it's maybe 1/3 offhand; the rest have maybe 1 or 2 in their deck), Terraforming is blank for the first several turns, and at most he plays 2 villain cards every other round, compared to La Capitan having at least two every single round until you can get the Boat to stay dead, and 1 more if Mable comes out.  My second game against Omnitron was only three heroes (granted one of them was Unity, but I was playing her for the first time, and she lost all her cards in play one round); I was deliberately trying to assemble a team that he'd have a fair chance of whomping, and he still rolled over in thoroughly pathetic fashion.  Flechettes is an extremely strong card, but it's pretty much the only thing in his deck I fear, unless I'm playing a hero who relies on Equipment.  Maybe it's just that Visi is his Kryptonite, but I don't buy it.  I think he's weaker than Baron Blade, and probably about equal with Gloomy (the Cultists are definitely meaner than Omni's silly little Drones, one of which is like the Explosive but with 1/3-1/5 the HP, and both of them only hit the single highest hero there is, which is pretty much "not even trying" compared to the minions of Voss, Dawn or Dreamy).

McBehrer:

That being said, KISMET? Really? She's already a 2, and a fairly low one at that.

The book lists her at 3, and I think that seems valid.  She made me sweat; ironically, she lost because luck was on my side, as she repeatedly failed to resolve Karmic Disjunction.  Had that actually landed, though…one time I started resolving it by mistake, and ALL FOUR of the cards were Jinxes, which would have meant her attack was +4 damage, and it hits all heroes.  At the very least, she's a high 2, but I could believe 3…and conceptually, she doesn't deserve to be that solid.  She's just a punk kid with a stolen gewgaw which makes her lucky; instead, she ends up as this psycho-kinetic wrecking bacll.  (Granted, it probably didn't help that we fought her in the Final Wasteland and she was using Abominable Snowmen to block our attacks.  And just when I was getting ready to take that card out, she busts out Lady Luck and I had to kill that instead, so we basically sat on our hands for two rounds until I draw my other Ongoing destroyer.)

I don't think they should make more easy villains; there are already plenty of those

Yeah, while I've had easy GAMES, Omnitron and maybe Baron Blade are the only easy VILLAINS IMO.  Anyone with minions is a steamroller, and even Ambuscade and Gloomy strike me as solid 2s, just because they have at least one way of dealing a huge amount of damage (Rocket Launcher from the High Ground, or the Ronway cultist with a +1 from one of the Relics).

and you don't HAVE to play against the hard ones your first time. It's a different issue than having Blade and Omnitron, who are so weak that once you learn the game you'll never touch them again.

This part I do agree with; they definitely deserved the upgrades.  But I think it ought to work in the other direction too.

posts.name: Envisioner

phantaskippy:

Also you used Visionary both times.  This makes sense of why you would believe Visionary too powerful and Omnitron too weak.  Visionary is phenomenal vs. Omnitron, even if he doesn't get EPE.  WtM isn't nearly as good vs. other decks, because often you take as much damage as you give, or more, On an EPE it is the win button.

Wrest the Mind wasn't a major factor in either of those wins.  The first, non-advanced win was largely due to four heroes getting Legacy's damage boosts, but in the second, Visionary utterly dominated Omnitron with Precognition and Suggestion.  He has more situationally-weak cards than nearly any other villain - Precognition on Voss is nearly worthless, because you're usually just choosing which of three Minions to bring out, determining little other than whether you take cold damage or psychic.  But with Omnitron, she made him waste his turns replaying TechSing twice after all the equipment was already gone, and Brain Burned his destroyed Drones so that all he could recycle were a couple "fires at the start of the villain turn" Components, which were easily destroyed over and over.

I do plan to try Omnitron eventually with a non-Visionary party, just as I will never again play Fanatic against the Dreamer.  But I thought part of the idea with Sentinels was that "any hero group can beat any villain in any environment".  That ought to go both ways - any hero group ought to have to work at beating any villain in any environment.  Visionary seems to just be an "I win button" against Omnitron, and that's even worse than Fanatic vs. Dreamer, because Visi and Omni are in the same box.  There's no way they weren't playtested against each other, so maybe the designers could have made this match a little less one-sided.

I honestly don't have much trouble with minion heavy villains, Akash is the only one I really get steamrolled by, and that is becasue I love playing her in final wasteland.
